title: Gradient Is Not the Same as Loss
text: A gradient at a point tells you the slope of the loss function there, not the actual value of the loss at that point.

title: Check What Is Missing
text: Does knowing the gradient at theta $$=$$ $$11$$ uniquely determine L(theta $$=$$ 11)?

title: Use NA When the Value Is Ambiguous
text: Without the full loss function or enough constraints, multiple loss values at $${\theta}^1$$ could be possible, so the entry is NA.
